item.title: Beppu Tower — Guide
item.description: Beppu Tower, standing near the bayfront in central Beppu, is one of Japan’s classic ‘Tower Six’ observation towers, built in the 1950s during the postwar era of tower-building and designed by the same architect behind Tokyo Tower and others. A registered tangible cultural property, it has a charming retro, mid-century character. From its observation deck, visitors get a sweeping panorama over the city of Beppu spread along its bay, with the columns of white steam rising from the onsen districts across the townscape, the sweep of Beppu Bay, and the surrounding mountains including Mount Tsurumi behind.

item.title: Fukuoka Tower: Seaside City Views — Guide
item.description: Fukuoka Tower, standing on the Momochihama seaside in the western part of the city, is the tallest seaside tower in Japan at 234 metres. Its striking exterior is clad in around 8,000 half-mirrors that reflect the sky and sea, and by night it is lit up in seasonal illuminations. High-speed lifts carry you to observation decks at around 120 metres, where floor-to-ceiling windows give sweeping 360-degree views over Fukuoka city, the modern Momochi waterfront district, Hakata Bay and, on clear days, the surrounding mountains and islands — especially beautiful at sunset and after dark.

item.title: Roppongi Hills & Tokyo City View — Guide
item.description: Roppongi Hills is a large, modern urban development in the Roppongi district, centred on the 54-storey Mori Tower and a hub of shopping, dining, art and nightlife. Its main draw for visitors is the Tokyo City View observation deck near the top of the tower, which offers spectacular 360-degree panoramas over the city — with a superb view of Tokyo Tower lit up at night as its centrepiece, plus the Skytree, Tokyo Bay and, on clear days, Mount Fuji.

item.title: Sapporo TV Tower — Guide
item.description: The Sapporo TV Tower, standing at the eastern end of the city’s central Odori Park, is one of Sapporo’s most recognisable landmarks. Completed in 1957 and rising about 147 metres, this red-and-white steel tower has a distinctly retro, mid-century charm. Its main draw is the observation deck at around 90 metres, which offers a superb straight-line view westward down the length of green Odori Park to the mountains beyond, as well as panoramas over the grid-planned city.

item.title: Tokyo Tower — Guide
item.description: Tokyo Tower, standing 333 metres tall in the Shiba-koen district, is one of the city’s most beloved and enduring symbols. Painted in distinctive orange and white and inspired by the Eiffel Tower, it was completed in 1958 as a broadcasting tower and quickly became an icon of post-war Tokyo’s rebirth. Though now surpassed in height by the Skytree, Tokyo Tower retains a special nostalgic, retro charm. Two observation decks — the Main Deck at 150 m and the higher Top Deck at 250 m — offer sweeping panoramic views over the city, taking in landmarks, Tokyo Bay and, on clear days, Mount Fuji, and the views are especially romantic after dark when the city lights up.
